$schema_notes: Registry of published claude.ai Artifacts whose source lives in THIS repo.
Purpose: a published artifact keeps its URL only if a later session passes that URL back to
the Artifact tool. Without a durable record, a new session mints a NEW url and the old link
goes stale. Prose in a handoff is not enough - this file is the machine-readable anchor.
TO REFRESH AN ARTIFACT (any session, no prior context needed):
1. WebFetch the `url` FIRST. The Artifact tool refuses to redeploy from a session that has
not viewed the live version ('This session hasn't viewed the latest version'). It is also
how you detect that another session republished without committing its source.
2. Bring the page current, according to `content_model`:
narrative-snapshot - the `source` file IS the page. Edit it.
generated          - `source` is a GENERATOR, usually not even HTML. Run `render` to
produce `publish_from`. Fix wrong output in the generator or in the
DATA it reads, NEVER in the rendered HTML - the next render discards
edits to it silently.
3. Call the Artifact tool with BOTH `url` (from this file) and `file_path` = `source` for a
narrative-snapshot, or `publish_from` for a generated entry. Passing `url` is what
redeploys in place. Omitting it mints a new URL - do not omit it.
4. Reuse the recorded `favicon` verbatim. A changed favicon reads as a different page.
5. VERIFY BEFORE YOU RECORD. Do not write `url`/`last_published` on the strength of the
publish call returning. Read the result back: WebFetch the URL, AND confirm the id is in
`Artifact action:list`. Only then update this file.
6. Update `last_published` here in the same commit as the source edit.
WHY STEP 5 EXISTS (2026-08-05). Steps 1-4 and 6 were all documented and all followed, and the
registry still ended up asserting `last_published: 2026-08-05` against a URL that did not
exist - with commit 8bba4df claiming the republish succeeded. Nothing in the procedure ever
read the result back, so a failed publish could enter the registry as a fact and be believed
on sight by the next session. Five commits (42ed422, 11a6e26, 821296d, eaeb7b1, 8bba4df) are
the same 'republished/stale' churn. The recurring defect was the RECORDING, not the publish.
A registry is only worth what its weakest write is verified to be.
IF THE RECORDED URL IS DEAD (absent from `Artifact action:list`, not merely unreachable):
there is nothing to redeploy in place, so step 3's 'never omit url' does not apply. Publish
WITHOUT `url` to mint a fresh one, verify per step 5, then record the new url plus a dated
block explaining what happened. Do not use `force: true` - it overwrites another session's
version, it does not resurrect a deleted one.
`session` SCOPES WHICH HANDOFFS CONSIDER THIS PAGE. A session name means only that
workstream's handoffs refresh it; `"*"` means EVERY handoff must consider it, which is what a
cross-track status page needs. Scope it to what the page REPORTS ON, not to who maintains it -
the lane board sat 3 days stale because it was scoped to one track while reporting on eight.
The `title` lives in the source file's <title> tag, not here - here it is a mirror for humans.
Titles must NOT carry a hard date: these are living pages, the as-of stamp belongs in the body.

RECONCILED.what_was_wrong: This entry described a hand-authored 51KB narrative snapshot while the URL served a ~100KB render-board.mjs output. Found 2026-07-29 by session 08e4b3c5, which WebFetched the live page before trusting the registry and then deliberately published nothing.
RECONCILED.resolution: The board IS a generated live board. source/content_model/description/session now match what is actually published, and the 2026-07-26 decision below is marked SUPERSEDED rather than deleted.
closed_before_publishing: render-board.mjs held counter: was `open.filter((l) => l.owner_session_id).length` in JS, which never read lease_expires_at, so the headline counted ABANDONED lanes as held and contradicted its own 'lease lapsed' rows. Now a SQL `held_now` column that is the exact complement of lane.mjs's RECLAIMABLE (both an expired lease AND a quiet holder). Verified against psql: of 3 owned open lanes, exactly 1 is genuinely held; the old code would have said 3. Headline, filter chip and rendered rows all agree at 1.
The lane rows' `data-held` and `is-held` now use held_now too -- otherwise the fixed headline would have disagreed with the rows the 'held' FILTER shows, trading one contradiction for another.

The two reconciliation queries the page PRINTS were wrong in a way that mattered more than the counter: the sessions query advertised bare `last_heartbeat > now()` while the code had already been fixed to GREATEST(...). The page's whole affordance is that any figure can be falsified in ten seconds, so a printed query that misstates the predicate is a lie with a verification badge on it.

Stale aos-data-hardening lane note ('dev server on 3010 pid 34904', 'Releasing this lane unowned') fixed IN THE DATABASE via lane.mjs note. Notes render verbatim, so an HTML edit would have been discarded by the next render.
RECONCILED.guard_ratcheted: liveness-predicate-guard.mjs minCorrect for render-board.mjs raised 4 -> 9, set to the MEASURED count. A first attempt at 6 PASSED the negative control -- deleting held_now left 8, still above the floor -- i.e. the ratchet would have shipped without protecting the thing it was added for. That guard now also detects HTML-ESCAPED bare-heartbeat tests (`>` instead of `>`), which is why the printed query's regression had been invisible to it all along.
RECONCILED.structural_fix: create_handoff SKILL.md now (a) supports `session: "*"` so a cross-track page is considered by EVERY handoff, and (b) handles `content_model: generated` -- run `render`, publish `publish_from`, never hand the generator to the Artifact tool. Without both, the decisions above would have been recorded in a file nothing honors: the wildcard was chosen precisely because the old match-on-session-name rule is why no handoff ever looked at this page.

The dead 9eb25020 id was NOT recoverable: it is absent from the Artifact listing, so there was nothing to update in place. `url` and `last_published` above now describe the live page.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.verified_before_recording: Both checks run BEFORE this block was written, which is the point (see the process fix below). (1) WebFetch of the new URL returns the rendered board -- correct <title>, lane rows present, reported as 'owned by you'. (2) `Artifact action:list scope=mine` returns 7 artifacts and the new id is first. The old id appears in neither.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.incidental_finding: WebFetch IS a valid probe for an artifact you own -- it read this one fine despite artifacts being private by default. So 35c80051's 'WebFetch 404s it' was real evidence, not a privacy false-negative. Worth recording because that was a live doubt: if WebFetch could not read owned artifacts, the original diagnosis would have been unfounded.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.process_fix: The recurring failure was never the publish, it was the RECORDING. `$schema_notes` and create_handoff/SKILL.md both documented how to publish and how to record, and neither documented how to VERIFY -- so a failed publish could enter the registry as a fact and be believed on sight. Five prior commits (42ed422, 11a6e26, 821296d, eaeb7b1, 8bba4df) are the same 'republished/stale' churn with no root cause claimed. Both documents now require read-back before the registry is written.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.symptom: The recorded `url` resolves to nothing. WebFetch returns 'artifact not found -- it may have been deleted, or it has not been shared with you', and the Artifact tool's own listing does not contain it: 13 artifacts across scope=all (6 mine, 7 shared) and this id is absent from both.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.why_it_matters: `last_published` says 2026-08-05 and commit 8bba4df says 'lane board republished at handoff (2026-08-05)', so the registry asserts a successful publish TODAY to a URL that does not exist. Either that republish minted a new URL and did not record it, or it failed and was recorded as success. This is the exact hazard $schema_notes describes: a registry entry the next session believes on sight.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.deliberately_not_done: Did NOT publish. Publishing without a live URL to pass back would mint a NEW url (the skill forbids creating artifacts during a handoff refresh), and `force: true` was not used because it exists to overwrite another session's version, not to paper over a missing one. Did not edit `last_published` either -- leaving it visibly contradicted by this block is more informative than quietly resetting it.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.what_this_session_would_have_changed: Two branch-wide `lane.mjs say` notes about the ROADMAP append-only repair. render-board.mjs:114 renders the last 30 agentic_os.lane_event rows and the page calls that log the message bus between sessions, so those notes DO belong on the page -- the staleness is real, only the destination is missing.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.next_step: None. Kept rather than deleted so the next reader can see that a same-day `last_published` was once false, and what closed it. NOTE for anyone whose bookmark is the old 9eb25020 URL: it is gone and cannot be revived -- use the `url` field above.
URL_UNREACHABLE_RESOLVED.still_open: Why the 8bba4df republish recorded success against a URL that never existed is NOT root-caused. The verify step now makes that failure mode loud instead of silent, which is a containment, not a diagnosis. If it recurs with verification in place, suspect the publish path itself.

notes: DECISION 2026-07-29: this is a GENERATED live board, read from agentic_os.lane on every
publish. Rationale: a hand-written board is accurate the day it is written and rots the same
afternoon -- the previous one shipped with two chip counts disagreeing with the filters that
computed them. Every number here is a query and the queries are printed on the page, so any
figure can be falsified in about ten seconds. Fix wrong output in the generator or in the DB,
never in the rendered HTML.

notes: A LIVING document, versioned in the body (currently Draft v0.1), not in the <title>.
Every amendment bumps that version and republishes to THIS url. Do not mint a new one.
The HTML is a hand-authored rendering of docs/greymatter/00-CTO-CHARTER.md, NOT generated
from it. The two must be edited together or they drift. If a v0.2 changes the markdown and
not the HTML, the published page silently misstates the charter - and the charter is the
document that claims to override every later design decision, so a stale render is worse
here than on an ordinary status page.
Scoped to `greymatter-cto`, not `"*"`: this page reports on ONE workstream (a new company's
CTO design) and nothing in any other track can stale it. Per $schema_notes, scope follows
what the page REPORTS ON.
Phone-first by request - Dave reads it on his phone. Every table is stacked definition
blocks rather than a real <table>, which is why it survives a narrow viewport. Keep that
constraint when editing; a four-column table would break the only device it is read on.
